title: Frontier-System Constraint Atlas
summary: A five-corridor qualitative map connecting frontier demand and authorization to the power, water, workforce, permitting, construction, acceptance, qualification, and outcome gates that local receiving systems must clear.
map_question: Where do five evidence-dense frontier systems encounter shared local conversion constraints, and what exact downstream records would advance them?
interpretation_boundary: The map compares evidence stages and constraint classes. It does not rank systems, normalize unlike measures, establish readiness, or imply technological, economic, environmental, or institutional equivalence.

nodes.label: Southwest chips
nodes.note: Physical fab progress remains dependent on named power, water, workforce, equipment, qualification, and production evidence.

nodes.label: Northern Virginia compute
nodes.note: Forecast demand must pass contracts, grid construction, land, permits, water, energization, compliance, and measured effects.

nodes.label: Nevada lithium
nodes.note: Authorized and financed projects remain upstream of construction, commissioning, qualified material, sales, and sustained performance.

nodes.label: Florida Space Coast
nodes.note: Planning and site decisions must pass capital delivery, operator authority, service, mission use, and repeat performance.

nodes.label: Ontario housing
nodes.note: Targets and approvals must pass legal enactment, servicing, permits, starts, completions, and occupancy.

nodes.label: Accepted power and utility service
nodes.note: Requires project-specific agreements, completed assets, energization, metering, cost, and reliability.

nodes.label: Accepted water and environmental capacity
nodes.note: Requires allocation, built infrastructure, actual use, treatment, monitoring, compliance, and impact evidence.

nodes.label: Authority and public acceptance
nodes.note: Requires final legal instruments, condition satisfaction, operating authority, and locally legible effects.

nodes.label: Construction, acceptance, and qualification
nodes.note: The common downstream hinge between an authorized project and an accepted operating asset.

nodes.label: Compatible measured outcomes
nodes.note: Requires stable identity, stage, period, definition, denominator, method, and acceptance before comparison.

nodes.label: Five named local project files
nodes.note: Phase 61 binds TSMC Arizona, Toronto application 24 254930, Northern Virginia large-load delivery, the Space Coast authority stack, and Nevada lithium to exact downstream artifacts, dates or triggers, and stop rules.

links.note: Utility territory, rate, and system-plan evidence exists; named accepted capacity remains incomplete.
A named wastewater agreement exists while accepted infrastructure and measured use remain open.
Forecast, rate, and transmission records are strong; customer service and energization remain project-specific gates.
Local standards and permits expose authority layers while final policy and operating compliance remain open.
Water and environmental permits define obligations without establishing compliant operation.
Construction, commissioning, product qualification, customer acceptance, and sustained output remain incomplete.
Site, environmental, and operator authority are separate stages tied to named facilities and missions.
One shared asset is operational while many planned projects and services remain upstream of acceptance and use.
The selected project exposes the distinction between recommendation, Council action, enactment, and satisfied conditions.
The selected application still needs a matched permit, start, completion, and occupancy trail.
Accepted assets and compatible repeated results are prerequisites for cross-system outcome interpretation.
Named files make the next delivery artifact inspectable without advancing a project beyond its evidence.

what_this_map_supports: Five evidence-dense local systems share recurring receiving-system and downstream delivery gates.
Project-level power, water, authority, construction, acceptance, and qualification records are more useful than another upstream announcement.
The same evidence-stage vocabulary can improve reader navigation across unlike sectors.
Phase 61 adds five named local project files with exact artifacts, dates or reopening triggers, and stop rules.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not rank local systems or create a readiness, performance, risk, or value score.
It does not treat unlike legal instruments, projects, technologies, units, or outcomes as equivalent.
It does not establish spare capacity, project viability, accepted operation, causality, or local benefit.
next_records_needed: Named service agreements, completed utility assets, energization, metered use, and reliability.
Water allocation, built infrastructure, actual use, treatment, compliance, and impact records.
Construction completion, inspection, acceptance, commissioning, qualification, and operating evidence.
